samples.summary: Headless copy-paste path likely regressed, and the design doc was rewritten to match rather than the gap being addressed. The URL is now printed only when `open` *throws*; on a headless Linux box `open` resolves successfully after spawning `xdg-open` even when no browser exists, so `opened` stays true and the user sees only 'Opening browser for GitHub login...' followed by a 30-second timeout. The removed doc line ('also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments') was the documented affordance for exactly that case. If the intent is that headless users use `--api-key`, the login flow should say so on timeout rather than silently dropping the URL.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:68-82 `try { await open(oauthUrl); opened = true } catch {}` … `if (!opened) { print URL }`; docs/design/cli.md step 3 changed to '(printed for copy-paste only when the browser cannot be opened)'

samples.summary: Layering: `logSafeUrl` is a free function inline in the root `AppModule` rather than beside the other logging concerns (or in the auth module that owns the secrets it protects), and it blanket-redacts every `/auth` query string — including the benign `mode`/`port` diagnostics that make a CLI login traceable in the access log. A narrower allowlist (drop `nonce`, `code_challenge`, `code`, `state`; keep the rest) would keep the diagnostic value the surrounding doc says query strings are kept for.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:24-36 `function logSafeUrl(url: unknown)` returning `${path}?<redacted>` for any `/auth` path

verdict.reason: The finding claims the auth-flow change was documented only in a "parallel" doc and that the canonical design doc was not updated. rest-api.md is not parallel: docs/design/README.md:159 designates it as the canonical doc for "CLI auth endpoints", and it is a pre-existing README-linked subsystem doc. Every element the finding lists as undocumented is present there: nonce/code_challenge on GET /auth/github with the 400 on a malformed challenge (rest-api.md:334-346), the callback validating state first with a 401 when absent, before the user lookup (rest-api.md:351-361, 395), POST /auth/cli/exchange accepting `{ code, codeVerifier? }` (rest-api.md:362-373), the wafflebase_oauth_state cookie with httpOnly/SameSite=Lax/path=/auth/5-minute TTL (rest-api.md:347-350, 395), and the new /auth query-string redaction in the pino req serializer (rest-api.md:396, matching packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:28). cli.md:175-237 carries the companion login-flow design. The originating task names precisely these two docs as its doc deliverable (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:67) and no acceptance criterion (lines 96-110) mentions backend.md. backend.md's lines 146/312-313/348-349 are indeed as quoted and are now incomplete, but that is stale-detail hygiene in a doc whose CLI-auth slice README already assigns elsewhere (and `{ code }` remains valid since codeVerifier is optional per auth.dto.ts:16) — at most minor, not the "required design doc missing or parallel" major the rubric describes.

verdict.reason: The quoted artifacts exist as described — docs/design/cli.md:1129 adds the `Backend 4xx … | 1 | HTTP_ERROR` row, and ordinary commands (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:81,108,122,140,158) throw a plain `Error('HTTP <status>')` that outputError codes as 'ERROR' (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:42-48, asserted at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:476-480). It is nonetheless not blocking under the design-fit rubric. cli.md is a spec/proposal doc (front matter `target-version: 0.6.3`, Goals/Non-Goals per docs/design/template.md), and §10's Error Matrix is a target-state contract, not an as-shipped one: grepping packages/cli/src shows no implementation at all of PATH_NOT_FOUND, FILE_EXISTS, YORKIE_ERROR, FONT_LOAD_ERROR or INVALID_RANGE (rows at 1119, 1125, 1126, 1133, 1135), and the pre-existing 401/403→UNAUTHORIZED row (1127) is implemented only in login.ts:188 and ctx.ts:65 — the same partiality the finding attributes uniquely to the new row. Measured against this lens's `major` criteria: the originating issue's acceptance criteria (single-line envelope, `command` field, code/message behavior unchanged — docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:56-62) are untouched by this row; the doc change updates the canonical subsystem doc rather than creating a parallel one; nothing is duplicated and no Non-Goal is exceeded. What is left is a documentation-precision preference, which is minor/taste-grade under this rubric and does not block.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual premise — that one of the two bundled efforts is "unrequested scope" with no mappable acceptance criterion — is contradicted by the repository. Both halves are chartered with their own plans, tests and acceptance criteria: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:1-3,56-61 ("Issue: #661", three acceptance criteria, plus a scope note at 19-31 justifying the emitter conversion) and docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:32-75,96-111 (plan, out-of-scope list, five acceptance criteria covering nonce echo, PKCE S256, browser state cookie, /auth redaction). The shared-branch decision the finding treats as accidental creep is explicitly recorded and reasoned at 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:24-30 ("It rides the #661 branch again (PR #786)... the two touch login.ts from opposite ends... splitting them now would mean two PRs whose only conflict is that file"), naming the same login.ts intersection the reviewer identified. Design-doc discipline holds for both, folded into the canonical subsystem docs rather than parallel files: docs/design/cli.md:168 (§3.1 login) and :1082-1112 (§9 envelope), docs/design/rest-api.md:334-366,396 (nonce/PKCE, /auth log redaction risk row), both linked at docs/design/README.md:159-160. The code the finding describes does exist (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:58,75,118,156; packages/backend/src/auth/*), so this is not a not-present refutation — it is that the described defect (unrequested scope) is disproven by the charters. Under this lens's rubric a major requires citing a failed acceptance criterion, missing/parallel design doc, duplicated module, or exceeded Non-Goal; the finding cites none and admits it cannot ("No originating issue accompanied this review, so I cannot map either half to an acceptance criterion"). What remains is a PR-granularity preference, which the rubric classifies as minor/non-blocking.

finding.summary: Two independently-tracked issues are landed in one change, against the task plan's own instruction to keep them apart
finding.evidence: The loopback task doc states: "A first attempt at this shipped inside the #661 error-envelope branch and was reverted for landing half-done ... This is that work done as its own change." (docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:17-22). The diff nevertheless contains BOTH the loopback/PKCE work (backend auth guard/store/controller, login.ts) and the whole #661 error-envelope + `command` attribution refactor (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md), touching ~30 CLI files. The two features share no dependency: `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope` are unrelated to the nonce/PKCE binding. Bundling makes the security-critical auth change hard to review and hard to revert independently — precisely the failure mode the loopback task doc says was already hit once.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise — that the loopback task plan instructs the two workstreams be kept in separate changes — is not present in the repository. The reviewer quotes lines 17-22 and stops immediately before the section that decides the question. `docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:24-30` is a "Where it landed" section stating: "It rides the #661 branch again (PR #786), not a separate one. What was wrong the first time was *half-done work* riding along, not the sharing of a branch: the two touch `login.ts` from opposite ends (the OAuth handshake vs. the failure envelope), so splitting them now would mean two PRs whose only conflict is that file." The plan therefore explicitly anticipates, records, and justifies exactly the co-landing the finding calls a violation. The reviewer additionally misquotes line 21-22 as "This is that work done as its own change"; the actual text is "This is that work redone in full — plan, tests, and docs of its own" — a completeness requirement, not a branch-separation one. The paired lessons doc (20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-lessons.md:12-23) likewise attributes the earlier revert to a half-implemented two-sided protocol change ("The first attempt made the CLI *require* an echo only the new backend sends"), not to branch bundling. No repo-level rule supplies the missing instruction either: CONTRIBUTING.md:11-17 and :59-69 require a design doc plus a task plan per change and explicitly permit design and code in the same PR, and greps for one-PR/one-issue/separate-branch language in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/tasks/README.md return nothing. Both workstreams carry their own complete, tracked doc set (todo + lessons for each), so design-doc discipline is satisfied on both sides. Both feature bodies do exist in the tree (formatter.ts/backendErrorEnvelope consumers; login.ts nonce/PKCE), so the co-landing is factually real — but it is the documented, sanctioned arrangement rather than a deviation from it. Under this lens's rubric, branch/PR granularity matches none of the `major` kinds (unmet acceptance criterion, missing or parallel design doc, duplicated module, breached Non-Goal), and the envelope work is not unrequested scope creep since it is driven by its own tracked issue #661 with its own plan and acceptance criteria; absent the not-present ground it would at most be `minor` process hygiene, which never blocks.

finding.summary: `login` labels every backend failure `UNAUTHORIZED`, contradicting the documented Error Matrix (5xx → SYSTEM) and the exit-code column
finding.evidence: `failFromBackend` is called with a hard-coded `code: 'UNAUTHORIZED'` fallback at login.ts:84, :101 and :120 regardless of status — the workspaces call at :118-123 even interpolates `HTTP ${wsRes.status}` into the message while still coding it `UNAUTHORIZED`, so a 500 from `/workspaces` is reported to an agent as an auth failure. docs/design/cli.md §10 (line 1117-1118) specifies `Backend 401/403 → exit 2, UNAUTHORIZED` and `Backend 5xx or network → exit 2, SYSTEM`; these paths exit 1 and never emit SYSTEM. Since #661's whole point is that agents branch on `code`, introducing a wrong-but-stable code on the first command an agent runs works against the acceptance criterion it is meant to serve.

verdict.reason: The finding's core claim — that `login` hard-codes `code: 'UNAUTHORIZED'` for every backend failure — is not present in this repository. `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` defines `codeForStatus` (lines 187-191) mapping 401/403→UNAUTHORIZED, >=500→SYSTEM, otherwise HTTP_ERROR, and `failFromBackend` (206-219) uses it, exiting 2 for UNAUTHORIZED/SYSTEM and 1 for HTTP_ERROR. The three call sites (98-104, 116-118, 132-138) pass only a fallback *message*, never a code; the `/workspaces` site interpolates `HTTP ${wsRes.status}` into the message but still derives the code from status, so a 500 there yields SYSTEM + exit 2, not an auth failure. This conforms to docs/design/cli.md §10 rows 1127-1129 and the explicit login row at 1130 ("`login`: exchange / `me` / `workspaces` rejected | 1/2 | (status-derived)"). The cited line numbers (84, 101, 120) correspond to the callback wait, a message argument, and a JSON cast respectively — not code literals.
